If the request supplies usernames as an array (usernames[]=a), Rails returns an Array, and Array has no `split` method... actually Array does not respond to split, so NoMethodError → unhandled 500. The mechanism is plausible and grounded in the new controller code, though the practical severity is low (malformed/tampered param on an admin-only endpoint, and the actual client sends a comma-joined string). Cannot fully verify real-world impact from the diff alone.

judged_text: add_members calls params.require(:usernames).split(",") without type-checking, so a request supplying usernames as an array (usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b or a JSON array body) raises NoMethodError: undefined method 'split' for Array and returns an unhandled 500. An admin (or any client tampering with parameter encoding) gets a raw 500 instead of a 4xx validation error; the failure is silent-server-error rather than a handled input-validation path, and the same array-shaped param is exactly what the client-side user-selector can naturally emit.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff adds `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. If the request supplies `usernames` as an Array (e.g., `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), `params.require(:usernames)` will return an Array and `.split` will raise `NoMethodError`, producing an unhandled 500. The diff contains no type-checking/coercion or rescue to return a 4xx validation error instead.
